Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

as you know phrase

also as you well know, you know (as you are aware)

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.18: Epicūrus, homō, ut scīs, voluptārius (Lewis & Short s.v. voluptārius)
Sen. Ep. 83.4: ūnus mihi sufficit Pharius, puer, ut scīs, amābilis
Traupman 213: ut satis scīs

ut scīs

parenthetic; ut with the indicative

Examples

  • nam, ut scīs, jam prīdem istum cantō Caesarem

    for, as you know, I have long been singing the praises of that CaesarCic. Q. Fr. 2.11.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. cantō)

  • Ut satis scīs, mihi hodiē obsōnandum est.

    As you well know, I have to go shopping today.Traupman 213

See also as, apparently.

SourcesLewis & Short: scio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 213.
